title: Normalized fibre comparisons, common-stage descent and rank loci
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $\ell$ a prime invertible in $k$, and $X$ a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and finite intermediate fields $E\subset L$ over $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Write $A_E=\mathcal O_E$, choose a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and put $B_{E,X}=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(A_E/\varpi_E^n)_X$ and $E_X=B_{E,X}[1/\varpi_E]$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. These are the continuous completed coefficient sheaves on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use the derived-complete constructible integral categories with compatible etale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], their raw rationalizations $D^b_c(X,E)$ [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], their bounded localized standard t-structures [prop-weil-localized-tstructure], and the pair category $D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], with the finite scalar functors $T_{L/E}$ and associators of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension].

For every such scheme $Z$, use its finite-stage heart fibres $\omega_{\bar z,E}$ with normalized lattice-limit and fractional-map prescriptions [lem-per-adic-normalized-fibre-exactness]. Let $g:Y\to X$ be a morphism between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and put $\bar x=g\bar y$. Use the actual completed rational pullback and its restriction $g^*$ to standard hearts [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback, lem-per-adic-stratified-pullback-texact]. There are natural isomorphisms
$$\omega_{\bar y,E}(g^*F)\cong\omega_{\bar x,E}(F),\qquad
\omega_{\bar x,L}(T_{L/E}F)\cong\omega_{\bar x,E}(F)\otimes_E L.$$
On normalized etale systems the first comparison is the inverse limit of the finite-level pullback-stalk comparisons followed by inversion of $\varpi_E$. The second is the finite integral scalar-limit comparison followed by inversion of the uniformizers. They respect quotient transitions, identity morphisms, composition of scheme morphisms, successive coefficient extensions and their scalar associators; the square combining pullback with scalar extension commutes. These comparisons are independent of the local lattice charts.

There is an induced fibre functor on the common-stage heart [lem-per-adic-common-stage-truncations] with value $\omega_{\bar x,E}(F)\otimes_E\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ on $(E,F)$. It is exact; the family of all such fibres is jointly conservative and detects zero morphisms and short exact complexes. The displayed pullback comparisons descend to these fibres.

Every finite-stage heart object admits a finite locally closed stratification on which its continuous realization is lisse, and on each such stratum $x\mapsto\dim_E\omega_{\bar x,E}(F)$ is well defined independently of the geometric point over $x$ and locally constant with finite image. Every geometric fibre over a fixed underlying point is isomorphic as an $E$-vector space, without a specified canonical isomorphism. The rank loci refine that stratification to a finite stratification, and the positive-rank strata give exactly the nonzero-fibre locus, a constructible subset [def-weil-constructible-subset]. These assertions also hold for common-stage heart objects with $E$ replaced by $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$; finite coefficient extension preserves ranks and the nonzero-fibre loci.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4, Definitions 6.8.3 and 6.8.6, Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15; finite quotient pullback/scalar comparisons and lisse ranks

proof.text: Identify the finite-stage heart with constructible continuous $E_X$-modules using the t-exact equivalence $J_X$. Choose a lisse stratum through $\bar x$ and an affine etale lattice chart there. Write $N_\bullet$ for its normalized finite-free etale reduction system and $M_{\bar x}=\varprojlim_n(N_n)_{\bar x}$. The normalized fibre is $M_{\bar x}[1/\varpi_E]$, and an integral system map divided by $\varpi_E^a$ acts as $\varpi_E^{-a}\varprojlim u_n$. The reduction equivalence reconstructs the chosen lisse lattice from $N_\bullet$. All subsequent local computations use precisely these quotient and localization maps; they make no claim about arbitrary pro-etale stalks commuting with inverse limits.

For a finite-level etale module sheaf $H$, let $c_{g,H}:(g^{-1}H)_{\bar y}\to H_{\bar x}$ be the inverse-image stalk isomorphism. It is linear: naturality applied to multiplication by any coefficient gives $c_{g,H}(as)=a c_{g,H}(s)$. Its germ formula sends the germ of a pulled section back to its original germ. Hence it commutes with every quotient transition; the identity and composite-pullback comparisons agree because both send each pulled germ to that same original germ. For any finite coefficient homomorphism $R\to R'$, the stalk scalar comparison sends $a\otimes s_{\bar x}$ to $(a\otimes s)_{\bar x}$. Pulling back this germ and then applying $c_g$ gives $a\otimes s_{\bar x}$ as well. Since these tensors generate stalk scalar extension, this proves the finite-level pullback/scalar square, including non-flat quotient homomorphisms.

source.place: Stacks Tag 03Q1, etale-cohomology.tex, lemma-stalk-pullback (3), germ formula; sheaf scalar stalk formula

proof.text: Apply the previous step to every $N_n$. The maps $c_{g,N_n}$ form an isomorphism of inverse systems, so their inverse limit is an isomorphism $\varprojlim_n(g^{-1}N_n)_{\bar y}\cong M_{\bar x}$. Invert $\varpi_E$ to define $\alpha_{g,F}:\omega_{\bar y,E}(g^*F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{\bar x,E}(F)$. This computes the specified completed rational pullback: the lisse reduction comparison commutes with module pullback, $J$ identifies completed rational pullback with derived module inverse image, and stratified pullback t-exactness identifies its local finite-free degree-zero model on $Y\times_X S$. The pulled chart $U\times_X(Y\times_XS)$ is etale and affine over the stratum $Y\times_XS$ but need not be an affine scheme; replace it by an affine open neighbourhood of the lift $(\bar u,\bar y)$, which leaves the stalks at that point unchanged, so it is an affine etale lattice chart of the pulled stratum as the normalization requires. Thus the calculation is made on the actual pullback of the chosen lattice chart, even when $g$ is not flat and that inverse-image stratum is empty away from $\bar y$. For a map $u/\varpi_E^a$, the two routes are $\varpi_E^{-a}\varprojlim c_g u_n$ and $\varpi_E^{-a}\varprojlim u_n c_g$, equal by naturality. This proves naturality in the whole finite-stage heart.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4; Remark 6.8.15, explicit module inverse image

proof.text:
Put $A=A_E$, $D=A_L$, $t=\varpi_E$, $v=\varpi_L$. Use the scalar system prescribed for lisse sheaves: at level $m$ it is $N_{n(m)}\otimes_{A/t^{n(m)}}D/v^m$, where $n(m)=\lceil m/e\rceil$ and $e$ is the ramification index. Finite scalar stalk comparison and adic reconstruction identify its stalk with $M_{\bar x}\otimes_A D/v^m$. Since $M_{\bar x}$ is finite free, $M_{\bar x}\otimes_A D$ is finite free over $D$; reconstruction over $D$ therefore makes the canonical map
$$M_{\bar x}\otimes_A D\longrightarrow\varprojlim_m(M_{\bar x}\otimes_A D/v^m)$$
an isomorphism. This is a statement about finite modules, not tensor commuting with an arbitrary inverse limit. This system is that of the actual $T_{L/E}F$: $T_{L/E}$ is completed integral coefficient change followed by localization, and on representatives $J_L(T_{L/E}QK)=L_X\otimes^L_{B_{L,X}}(K\otimes^L_{B_{E,X}}B_{L,X})\cong L_X\otimes_{E_X}J_E(QK)$ by balancing, the comparison of $J$ with finite coefficient extension; on the chart the lattice $N$ is locally free, so $N\otimes_{B_{E,X}}B_{L,X}$ is a lisse lattice of $T_{L/E}F$, and the lisse system comparison identifies its reduction modulo $v^m$ with the displayed level-$m$ term ($t^{n(m)}\in v^mD$). Its inverse followed by localization gives
$$\beta_{L/E,F}:\omega_{\bar x,L}(T_{L/E}F)\xrightarrow{\sim}M_{\bar x}[1/t]\otimes_E L.$$
Indeed both localized modules are canonically $M_{\bar x}\otimes_A L$. The scalar stalk maps and the reconstruction maps are natural, so the formula also commutes with every fractional lattice map.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4); finite integral scalar comparison, Stacks Tags 09B8, 031D, 00MA

proof.text: The comparisons have the required coherence with the specified functor comparisons. On a quotient, scalar extension maps a pure tensor $(s\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $s\otimes ab$; pulling back changes only the germ of $s$, and the map of step 2 sends that pulled germ back to $s$. Consequently both routes through the mixed pullback/scalar square agree on every pure tensor. In a tower $E\subset L\subset P$ both scalar routes send $(s\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $s\otimes ab$; identity extension sends $s\otimes1$ to $s$. These are the balancing associators used by $T$, not arbitrary chosen isomorphisms. Quotient projections commute with all of these formulas. Equality after every finite quotient implies equality of maps into the inverse limit, and localization preserves the equations. The composite-pullback equation similarly follows from the germ equation in step 2. This proves the quotient, identity, scheme-composition, coefficient-composition and mixed-square equations for $\alpha$ and $\beta$.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4, quotient-normalized comparisons; Remark 6.8.15, balancing maps

proof.text: The formulas descend from the chosen charts. On a common etale refinement, a change of lisse lattice is an isomorphism of rational lisse realizations; full faithfulness of raw lattice rationalization represents it by a fractional integral map. Naturality just proved says that conjugating $\alpha$ or $\beta$ by that map gives the comparison computed from the other lattice. The same argument applies to changes of chart and adapted stratification using the normalized fibre identifications. Explicitly, after clearing the finitely many denominators of a comparison, the equality is the equality of the finite-level diagrams, multiplied by the same inverse power of $\varpi_E$. If another fractional representative is chosen, equality in the localized Hom group means some power of $\varpi_E$ kills their difference; its rational fibre map is therefore zero. Thus no lattice, chart, stratification or denominator choice survives.

For a heart pair $(E,F)$ set $V_{\bar x}(E,F)=\omega_{\bar x,E}(F)\otimes_E\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. If $[M,u]:(E,F)\to(L,G)$ is represented at a common field $M$, use $\beta_{M/E}$ and $\beta_{M/L}$ to identify the two sides with $\omega_{\bar x,M}(T_{M/E}F)\otimes_M\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and $\omega_{\bar x,M}(T_{M/L}G)\otimes_M\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and apply $\omega_{\bar x,M}(u)\otimes_M\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ between them. Step 5 says exactly that replacing $u$ by $a\,T(u)\,a^{-1}$ at a larger field leaves this map unchanged. The pair-category equivalence relation and common-stage calculus therefore give a well-defined additive functor, with identities and composition computed at one common stage. Common-stage truncations say every object of the heart is isomorphic to such a finite-stage heart pair. Transport along these isomorphisms extends the construction to that heart; the functorial equations make this independent up to its natural comparison isomorphism.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14, finite coefficient descent; pair-category and truncation formulas

proof.text: Finite-stage inclusions into the pair category preserve kernels and cokernels of heart maps: complete a map at that stage to a cone triangle, compute its kernel and cokernel as $H^{-1}$ and $H^0$ of the cone, and use the common-stage cone definition and truncation comparisons. Thus kernels, images, cokernels and homology of any finite heart complex are represented by the corresponding finite-stage objects after a common enlargement. A zero object represented at a finite stage becomes zero at a further stage: apply the equality criterion of common-stage calculus to its identity being zero. Hence any short exact sequence in the common heart is short exact at some finite enlargement (kill its endpoint and middle homology obstructions there). At that stage $\omega_{\bar x,M}$ is exact, and extension $-\otimes_M\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ is exact. Applying these to that short exact sequence proves exactness of $V_{\bar x}$. This also verifies exactness for heart objects originally given only up to isomorphism.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14 and common-stage cones/truncations; heart cone kernel and cokernel formulas

proof.text: Extension of vector-space scalars to a field is faithful and reflects zero: choose a basis, so $W\otimes_M\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\cong\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell^{(B)}$, and $w\mapsto w\otimes1$ is injective. Naturality of this injection also detects zero linear maps; exactness identifies the scalar-extended homology with the homology after scalar extension. Represent an object, a morphism, or a short complex over a common heart stage. If all its common-stage fibres vanish, are zero maps, or are short exact, respectively, these elementary scalar tests imply the same finite-stage fibre assertions. Finite-stage normalized fibres detect zero objects, zero maps and short exactness. Passing the resulting assertions through the common-stage inclusion gives the claimed detection. Applied to the kernel and cokernel of a map, zero-object detection and exactness show joint conservativity as well.

source.place: Finite-stage normalized fibre detection; finite-diagram descent and elementary basis argument

proof.text: For a common-stage heart object represented by $(E,F)$, tensor $\alpha_{g,F}$ with $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. The mixed-square equation of step 5 makes this independent of enlarging $E$ and compatible with the action on $[M,u]$ in step 7. Consequently it defines the displayed pullback comparison on common-stage fibres, natural in all common-stage maps. Identity and composite-pullback equations descend as well, since each finite diagram is represented over one field and the equations already hold there. The descended pullback is the actual common-stage pullback supplied by stratified pullback t-exactness.

By the heart realization, choose a finite locally closed stratification with lisse continuous realization on each stratum $S$. To apply the existing lisse-rank theorem, identify its pulled condensed coefficient ring with the continuous coefficient ring, and hence with $E_S=B_{E,S}[1/\varpi_E]$. Transport of a module along this ring isomorphism preserves its finite-free trivializations. The rank theorem supplies clopen rank loci in $S$ and a finite range because $S$ is noetherian, hence quasi-compact. Its rank equals the normalized fibre dimension: on an etale lattice chart the normalized reduction equivalence gives finite locally free $N_n$ of the same local rank $r$, the reconstructed lattice has that rank, and its inverse-limit fibre is free of rank $r$. After inversion it is $E^r$. This uses only the finite-level stalk of a constant module, which is that module. Thus every geometric point over $x\in S$ has dimension $r(x)$, independent of chart and geometric point. Two such fibres are isomorphic as $E$-vector spaces by choosing bases of their equal dimension; this asserts no canonical choice of path or isomorphism.

For each of the finitely many $S$, intersect it with its finitely many nonempty clopen rank loci. These subsets are locally closed in $X$, pairwise disjoint and cover $X$, so they are a finite stratification. A fibre is nonzero exactly when its rank is positive, since it is finite-dimensional. Thus the nonzero-fibre locus is the union of the positive-rank strata; a finite union of locally closed subsets in this noetherian space is constructible. For a finite field extension, an $E$-basis of a fibre becomes an $L$-basis of its scalar extension, so step 4 proves rank and nonzero-locus invariance. For any common-stage heart object, choose a finite-stage representative as in step 7; the same basis argument gives equal rank after extension to $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. The resulting strata and nonzero locus therefore have all the asserted properties, independent of the representative, since the functor sends isomorphisms to fibre isomorphisms.

I added the bridge J_L∘T ≅ L_X⊗_{E_X}J_E by balancing, with T defined as integral change of coefficients followed by localization, and the lattice N⊗_{B_E}B_L. Its uses gain the realization node and prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension, both already in proof_deps. In step 3 the pulled chart U×_X(Y×_X S) is affine over the stratum but need not be an affine scheme; I shrink it to an affine neighbourhood of (ū,ȳ).
